title: Week 21 Check-In · The Whipping Boy
description: This week the prince took a whipping without a sound, the boys walked through the fair and escaped through the sewer, and the story ended in the king’s throne room. You practiced prepositional phrases, the word parts re, un, pre, dis, and mis, and homophones. Show what you know!

questions.text: Write one sentence that uses to and one sentence that uses two.
What does the prince do differently in this passage compared to how he acted at the start of the book?
The passage says the prince set his jaw “just as Jemmy always had.” What do you think this means? What is changing for the prince?
Do you think the prince has truly changed, or is he just acting differently because of the situation? Use details from the book to support your opinion.

Model sentence: “For the first time in his life, the prince took a whipping himself, and like Jemmy, he did not make a sound.” Notice how the author shows the change through what the prince does NOT do. Write your own sentence about a character changing using this technique.
Write 2–3 sentences describing how the prince changed from the beginning of the book to the end. Use specific details.

passage.title: Reading passage (summary of Ch. 16)
passage.text: Hold-Your-Nose Billy thought the prince was only the whipping boy, so he raised Captain Nips’s horsewhip and brought it down on the prince’s back. Jemmy had dreamed of seeing the prince whipped, but now he found no satisfaction in it. “Bawl out!” he shouted. The prince set his jaw, just as Jemmy always had, and not a sound escaped his lips. He only got ready for the next blow.
